name: Low-Bandwidth Knowledge and Operations OS
promise: Preserve context and expose the next safe action when bandwidth is low.
completion_criteria: One SourceRecord path preserves capture, checksum, provenance, retrieval citation, and projection ownership.
Generated Observer notes cannot be ingested back as new canonical sources.
JARVIS presents and approves actions without duplicating storage or domain logic.
Unique Ryos and master-plan behavior is ported or rejected before their runtimes are retired.
Daily operation retains deterministic fallbacks when providers or credentials are unavailable.

waves.objective: Acquire live dotfiles into authentic PKos CAS, normalize into SQLite, and generate fenced Observer projection.
waves.acceptance: The source is acquired into authentic PKos raw object storage, normalized into SQLite items and chunks, projected into a fenced Observer note, and mutation protection holds.
waves.runtime_followup: Scale real day-to-day intake stream through the live PKos capture path into the permanent personal vault, and accumulate the authentic accepted uses that an adoption claim requires. The invocation itself is now proven: the receipt retains the argv, exit code, duration, and host-recomputed digests of the PKos modules that ran, so the claim is no longer capped at what the projection could show.

waves.objective: Inventory Ryos core files and master-plan specs read from live source against dotfiles and Observer.
waves.acceptance: Ryos and master-plan files are enumerated from the working trees and each catalogued behavior carries a port target, explicit rejection, or preserved historical owner. No port is executed.
waves.runtime_followup: Execute the assigned ports in dotfiles and back each with a test, or record the rejection.

waves.objective: Model a JARVIS action preview receipt with an approval boundary in the suite-local engine, against a fingerprinted JARVIS source.
waves.acceptance: The preview receipt requires human approval, is dry-run only, and creates no duplicate state. JARVIS backend source files are inspected, not invoked.
waves.runtime_followup: Drive a real JARVIS action through preview, approval, execution receipt, failure, and recovery over owned APIs or file contracts.

waves.objective: Ingest three authentic donor README sources through PKOS capture with fenced Observer projections.
waves.acceptance: A batch of at least three donor README sources produces content-addressed SourceRecords, each cited and fenced from re-ingestion.
waves.runtime_followup: Run the real day-to-day daily-notes stream through the live PKos capture path into the permanent vault.

waves.objective: Formalize the disposition of the live Ryos and master-plan inventory: name port targets, superseded features, and canonical anchors.
waves.acceptance: A disposition proposal is recorded from the live O2 inventory with dotfiles and PKos named as sole operational anchors and at least two port candidates assigned. Duplicate decisions remain open at close_on_verification. No code is ported and no donor is retired.
waves.runtime_followup: Close the named duplicate decisions against a verified migration, port the named launcher features into dotfiles, and retire the duplicate donors.

waves.objective: Generalize the modelled JARVIS action pattern to multiple commands with a full approval and receipt lifecycle in the suite-local engine.
waves.acceptance: Preview, human approval gate, execution receipt, and fail-closed rejection of unapproved execution are verified across a multi-action surface with JARVIS source inspected and zero disk mutations.
waves.runtime_followup: Run the same lifecycle against real JARVIS commands that perform actual side effects.
